\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আয়োজন} (āyojôn)}{আয়োজন (āyojôn)}]{\bn{আয়োজন} (āyojôn) — preparations (for an event); the organising}

\label{lesson:BN-C378-ayojon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to surpass, then the Bengali for to accomplish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আয়োজন}}
\textbf{\bn{আয়োজন}} — \emph{āyojôn} — \textquotedblleft{}preparations (for an event); the organising\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বিয়ের} \bn{আয়োজন} \bn{সময়মতো} \bn{শেষ} \bn{না} \bn{হলে} \bn{খুব} \bn{ঝামেলা} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{biyer āyojôn sômôymôto shesh nā hôle khub jhāmelā hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the wedding preparations aren't finished in time, there will be a lot of trouble.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আয়োজন}} (\emph{āyojôn}) is Sanskrit \emph{āyojana}, a joining or collecting (Monier-Williams). The Bengali sense, all the preparations and arrangements for an event, is not one the dictionary gives; it goes with \bn{করা}: \bn{বিয়ের} \bn{আয়োজন} \bn{করা}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āyojôn}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āyojôn}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{biyer āyojôn sômôymôto shesh nā hôle khub jhāmelā hôbe.} — If the wedding preparations aren't finished in time, there will be a lot of trouble.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to surpass, then the Bengali for to accomplish, then say \emph{āyojôn} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{আয়োজন} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Preparations (for an event); the organising\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অবিলম্বে} (ôbilômbe)}{অবিলম্বে (ôbilômbe)}]{\bn{অবিলম্বে} (ôbilômbe) — immediately; without delay}

\label{lesson:BN-C378-obilombe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to accomplish, then the Bengali for preparations (for an event).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অবিলম্বে}}
\textbf{\bn{অবিলম্বে}} — \emph{ôbilômbe} — \textquotedblleft{}immediately; without delay\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{জ্বর} \bn{বাড়লে} \bn{অবিলম্বে} \bn{ডাক্তার} \bn{ডাকো।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jbôr bāṛle ôbilômbe ḍāktār ḍāko.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the fever rises, call a doctor at once.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অবিলম্বে}} (\emph{ôbilômbe}) is Sanskrit \emph{a-} 'without' with \emph{vilamba}, delay (Monier-Williams), and the Bengali ending -\bn{এ}: 'without delay'. It is the word of notices and orders.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôbilômbe}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôbilômbe}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jbôr bāṛle ôbilômbe ḍāktār ḍāko.} — If the fever rises, call a doctor at once.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to accomplish, then the Bengali for preparations (for an event), then say \emph{ôbilômbe} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অবিলম্বে} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Immediately; without delay\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{মেয়াদ} (meyād)}{মেয়াদ (meyād)}]{\bn{মেয়াদ} (meyād) — a term; a period of validity}

\label{lesson:BN-C378-meyad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for preparations (for an event), then the Bengali for without delay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{মেয়াদ}}
\textbf{\bn{মেয়াদ}} — \emph{meyād} — \textquotedblleft{}a term; a period of validity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ভিসার} \bn{মেয়াদ} \bn{শেষ} \bn{হলে} \bn{তোমাকে} \bn{দেশে} \bn{ফিরতে} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bhisār meyād shesh hôle tomāke deshe phirte hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When your visa runs out, you will have to go back home.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{মেয়াদ}} (\emph{meyād}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{mīʿād}, an appointed time, which would have come into Bengali through Persian: the time a visa, a lease or a loan runs for. When it ends, \bn{মেয়াদ} \bn{শেষ} \bn{হয়}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{meyād}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{meyād}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhisār meyād shesh hôle tomāke deshe phirte hôbe.} — When your visa runs out, you will have to go back home.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for preparations (for an event), then the Bengali for without delay, then say \emph{meyād} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{মেয়াদ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A term; a period of validity\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{স্থগিত} \bn{করা} (sthôgitô kôrā)}{স্থগিত করা (sthôgitô kôrā)}]{\bn{স্থগিত} \bn{করা} (sthôgitô kôrā) — to postpone; to suspend}

\label{lesson:BN-C378-sthogito-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for without delay, then the Bengali for a period of validity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{স্থগিত} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{স্থগিত} \bn{করা}} — \emph{sthôgitô kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to postpone; to suspend\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আবহাওয়া} \bn{খারাপ} \bn{হলে} \bn{স্কুল} \bn{খেলাটা} \bn{স্থগিত} \bn{করবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ābôhāoyā khārāp hôle skul khelāṭā sthôgitô kôrbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the weather turns bad, the school will postpone the match.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{সভাটা} \bn{স্থগিত} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini sôbhāṭā sthôgitô kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{স্থগিত} \bn{করা}} (\emph{sthôgitô kôrā}) is Sanskrit \emph{sthagita}, covered or hidden (Monier-Williams), with \bn{করা}. Monier-Williams also gives closed and stopped or interrupted, the sense Bengali keeps: to put a match, a meeting or a plan on hold.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sthôgitô kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sthôgitô kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ābôhāoyā khārāp hôle skul khelāṭā sthôgitô kôrbe.} — If the weather turns bad, the school will postpone the match.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for without delay, then the Bengali for a period of validity, then say \emph{sthôgitô kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{তাগাদা} \bn{দেওয়া} (tāgādā deoyā)}{তাগাদা দেওয়া (tāgādā deoyā)}]{\bn{তাগাদা} \bn{দেওয়া} (tāgādā deoyā) — to chase up; to press (someone) for}

\label{lesson:BN-C378-tagada-deoya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a period of validity, then the Bengali for to postpone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{তাগাদা} \bn{দেওয়া}}
\textbf{\bn{তাগাদা} \bn{দেওয়া}} — \emph{tāgādā deoyā} — \textquotedblleft{}to chase up; to press (someone) for\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{কাজটা} \bn{না} \bn{হলে} \bn{ম্যানেজারকে} \bn{তাগাদা} \bn{দাও।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kājṭā nā hôle mænejārke tāgādā dāo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the work isn't done, chase up the manager.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{টাকার} \bn{জন্য} \bn{তাগাদা} \bn{দিলেন}, \emph{tini ṭākār jônyô tāgādā dilen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{তাগাদা} \bn{দেওয়া}} (\emph{tāgādā deoyā}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{taqāḍā}, a pressing demand, through Persian, with \bn{দেওয়া}: to keep reminding someone until it gets done.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tāgādā deoyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kājṭā nā hôle mænejārke tāgādā dāo.} — If the work isn't done, chase up the manager.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a period of validity, then the Bengali for to postpone, then say \emph{tāgādā deoyā} again
\end{itemize}
